scope: Existing hosted presets only; frozen Build2082 compared with current official public docs

protocol_profiles.name: chat_completions
protocol_profiles.statement: Request model/messages and nested tools[].function{name,parameters}; assistant tool_calls contain IDs and JSON argument strings; role:tool results reference tool_call_id. Stream choices[].delta may contain empty content, multiple indexed tool fragments, usage-only frames and a final marker. Preserve errors and distinguish absent usage from measured zero.

protocol_profiles.name: responses
protocol_profiles.statement: Use input items and flat function tool definitions. Return function_call_output linked by call_id. Parse typed output items to preserve content beyond output_text. SSE has text/argument deltas, output_item.done, completed, failed, incomplete and error. Preserve final native reasoning items; an in-progress encrypted item may be incomplete.

protocol_profiles.name: anthropic_messages
protocol_profiles.statement: Use top-level system, user/assistant content arrays, max_tokens, native tool input_schema and linked tool_use/tool_result blocks. Reassemble indexed JSON/thinking/signature deltas and require message_stop. Preserve entire assistant blocks unchanged for continuation.

protocol_profiles.name: gemini_generate_content
protocol_profiles.statement: Use model/method in the path and native contents/parts JSON. Tools use functionDeclarations, object args and functionResponse. Preserve Part metadata and opaque thoughtSignature values. Read native candidates, finishReason and usageMetadata; do not impose Chat delta envelopes.

claims.statement: Use POST /v1/responses. Organization/project headers are conditional for multi-organization or legacy-key selection, not universal API requirements.

Replay native output items, or use previous_response_id. With store:false or ZDR, encrypted reasoning is returned by default; the legacy include value reasoning.encrypted_content remains accepted. Preserve opaque fields, ordering and identities.

429 may mean temporary rate limiting, exhausted credits, or spend/usage limits. Inspect error.code. Rate errors and 503 overload require honoring Retry-After when present; retrying billing errors does not restore access.

OpenCode inference explicitly documents Authorization: Bearer for all API families, including Anthropic and native Gemini. The inference guide does not document x-api-key or x-goog-api-key aliases. /v1/models is a discovery path, not the documented inference base.

Go inference uses /inference/go/openai/v1/chat/completions or /responses, /inference/go/anthropic/v1/messages, and /inference/go/google/v1beta/models/<model>:generateContent (streamGenerateContent for streaming). The current Go table includes a Gemini contributor model on the native Google family; MiniMax and Qwen use Messages.

Console inference uses /inference/openai/v1/chat/completions or /responses, /inference/anthropic/v1/messages, and /inference/google/v1beta/models/<model>:generateContent. Its table routes Gemini to Google, GPT/Grok/Muse Spark to Responses, Claude and most Qwen to Messages, Qwen3.8 Max and the listed open models to Chat Completions. Use exact exceptions before prefixes.
POST /api/v1/chat/completions normalizes message/delta choices. HTTP-Referer and X-OpenRouter-Title are optional attribution headers; their absence is not a protocol failure.
Preserve complete, ordered reasoning_details for encrypted/summary blocks. Plain reasoning can be replayed as reasoning; reasoning_content is a documented alias here.

Ignore SSE comments. A stream may fail after HTTP 200 through a top-level error and finish_reason:error, including as its only event. The final usage frame repeats the terminal finish_reason with a content-free choice; it is not a second generation.
The documented OpenAI client and direct HTTP route use /v1/chat/completions. HTTP-Referer and X-Title are requested application attribution and explicitly shown as optional, not authentication.

Tool syntax is standard nested OpenAI function definitions, JSON argument strings and linked tool result IDs. The tool guide lists native Kimi-K2-Instruct and Qwen 3 family support; catalogue presence alone does not establish tool capability.

A 400 can mean a cold/loading model; 403 can mean gated-model access rather than a malformed key. 503 can mean model capacity exhaustion; the error guide recommends retrying the same request and reconsidering availability if it persists beyond three retries.

Use the documented OpenAI-compatible base and Chat Completions. Groq rejects logprobs, logit_bias, top_logprobs and messages[].name, and only supports n=1. Newer Responses support does not change Sylvia's selected Chat route.

Tool support is model-specific. Parsed reasoning uses message.reasoning; raw mode uses think tags and cannot be explicitly combined with tools or JSON mode. include_reasoning and reasoning_format are mutually exclusive. GPT-OSS effort supports low/medium/high; other families have their own values.

HTTP error bodies contain error.message/type. 429 is rate limiting; 500/502/503 can warrant delayed retry. The current error table also distinguishes 413 payload, 422 semantic/tool errors, and 498 Flex capacity.

Use /v1/chat/completions and exact provider/model IDs. Errors use an OpenAI-shaped envelope with Together-owned type/code values. Cached token usage can be nested in prompt_tokens_details or flat in usage.cached_tokens.
Chat streaming returns incremental deltas; tool patterns include multiple, parallel and sequential calls. Tool eligibility comes from the selected serverless/dedicated model, not the provider name.

Reasoning may be in reasoning or reasoning_content; replay it under the same key. Preserved-thinking blocks must retain the original sequence. Hybrid controls and allowed effort values vary; DeepSeek V3.1 tools require non-reasoning mode.

Official SDK examples use the root base URL, Chat Completions, streaming reasoning_content/content, nested function tools and role:tool results linked by tool_call_id. Thinking defaults on in the current guide. With tools present, replay reasoning_content from every earlier assistant turn, including turns without tool calls, or the API can return 400.

POST /v1/messages is the native API. anthropic-version and content-type are required. Current docs prefer Bearer credentials and explicitly retain x-api-key fallback; anthropic-workspace-id is required for multi-workspace keys and optional for ordinary single-workspace keys.

The stream consists of message_start, indexed content block start/delta/stop, message_delta and message_stop, with possible ping/error events. Tool input_json_delta is partial JSON. Thinking signatures arrive as signature_delta. Echo complete assistant content unchanged before the user tool_result.

Manual thinking requires budget_tokens >=1024 and normally less than max_tokens; newer models require adaptive thinking instead. Error handling distinguishes 429 rate/spend limits, 500, 504 and 529 overload; SSE errors can follow HTTP 200.

The direct preset correctly selects v1beta/openai/chat/completions, Bearer authentication, standard tools and streaming deltas. Google-specific thinking configuration lives in its documented extra_body.google extension; compatibility remains beta.

Native generateContent uses user/model contents[].parts, systemInstruction, functionDeclarations, functionCall object arguments and functionResponse objects. If a functionCall supplies an id, return the matching id. Part.thoughtSignature is an opaque base64 value for reuse. streamGenerateContent uses native candidate/parts responses, not Chat choices.

The current quickstart uses /v1/responses. Responses uses typed output items and function_call_output with call_id; stateful tool examples use previous_response_id. store defaults true; include requests encrypted reasoning. Direct OpenAI's automatic encrypted include guarantee is not stated for xAI.

The official Responses example sends text.format with type:json_schema, name, schema and strict:true. The Chat response_format envelope must be translated for this selected transport. Exact strict-omission fallback is not documented as identical to OpenAI.
The error guide separates authentication/permission, not-found, invalid body/media and 429 rate limiting. Do not retry invalid input as a connection failure.

POST /v1/chat/completions accepts model/messages/tools; streaming is data-only SSE ending in [DONE]. Preserve tool-call identity across assistant/tool turns; model support still governs available features.

When enabled, current reasoning returns content as ThinkChunk/TextChunk lists. Streaming can produce a thinking list, a mixed thinking/text list, then a plain string. Replay the complete assistant message including thinking chunks.

Official SDK setup uses ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.minimax.io/anthropic with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, so removing the saved /v1 before SDK construction is correct. It requires complete response.content replay, including thinking/text/tool_use. max_tokens includes thinking; undersized caps can end before text.
MiniMax's general error table separates retry-later conditions such as 1000/1001/1002/1024 from invalid credentials 1004, insufficient balance 1008 and invalid parameters 2013.
The ordinary platform documents /v1/chat/completions and standard tool-call/result loops. Its availability of additional API families does not require expanding this preset or switching to Kimi Code.

Kimi K3 and K2.7 Code always preserve thinking; replay every historical assistant message including reasoning_content unchanged. K2.6 preservation is optional. Effort/toggle fields differ by model; K3 uses top-level reasoning_effort and no thinking parameter.

The official streaming guide explicitly requires data:[DONE]; finish_reason:stop alone is insufficient. Tool fragments accumulate by index. include_usage sends a final empty-choices accounting frame; an interrupted stream can lack final usage.
The standard endpoint is /api/paas/v4/chat/completions. Coding Plan uses a separate endpoint. Accept-Language configures response language and has a default; it is not an additional credential.
Preserved Thinking is enabled using thinking.clear_thinking:false in extra_body. Replay the complete unmodified reasoning_content sequence, including prior assistant tool turns.

Interpret both HTTP status and business error.code. 429 includes rate overload (1302/1305) but also exhausted balance (1113) and plan/access problems; retrying every 429 as temporary throttling misstates the cause.

The Singapore shared base in Sylvia is documented. Beijing, Virginia, Hong Kong and workspace-specific domains have distinct bases; the key must match the selected region/workspace. Keep endpoint editability. Token/Coding Plan endpoints are separate services.

OpenAI-compatible HTTP requests use Chat Completions messages and standard error envelopes. SSE carries choices/delta, terminal finish_reason and [DONE]. Streaming tool arguments are fragments and the name arrives in the first tool fragment; thinking/tool constraints depend on model.

Use exact full Fireworks model/deployment identifiers. Streaming usage is included on the terminal finish_reason frame. Default context-overflow behaviour lowers max_tokens to fit; context_length_exceeded_behavior:error requests an error instead.

Streaming tool calls require accumulating all indexed argument fragments. Reasoning uses reasoning_content, with model-specific allowed effort values; GPT-OSS rejects none and integer effort, while MiniMax M3 has its own adaptive option.

Fireworks recommends backoff for 429/500/502/503/504 and fixing 400/401/404/422. Error-code documentation additionally distinguishes 402 payment, 408 timeout and 520 unknown errors. Dedicated 429 means deployment capacity; serverless 429 means rate/TPM limits.

Use exact shared model IDs or a dedicated endpoint ID in model. Standard stream:true is supported; do not send tool_stream. n=1 only. Tools plus response_format is model-dependent and rejected by GPT-OSS-120B.

Function tools support linked results, parallel calls and strict schemas on documented models. Strictness has model-specific schema limits; Qwen rejects pattern/minLength/maxLength in strict tool schemas. Streaming emits Chat delta content.

The SDK documents retrying connection failures, 408, 429 and >=500 with bounded exponential backoff. This is SDK policy, not a requirement to reproduce exactly two retries. Auth/permission/invalid-body errors remain distinct.
reasoning_content is documented in input messages. reasoning_history controls stripping or preservation with model-specific defaults; it does not disable reasoning computation.

For qwen-3.8-27b, clear_thinking false or omitted preserves historical assistant reasoning supplied in the conversation; true removes it. The documented output reasoning field does not justify arbitrary alternate input aliases.
On documented preserve_thinking-capable models, historical assistant reasoning_content is accepted and used when preservation is enabled. Missing reasoning history is allowed. Model defaults differ.
The inspected reasoning and API references establish returned reasoning, but no explicit general assistant-history scalar replay requirement or alias guarantee was found.

mismatches.title: OpenCode inference path mismatch
mismatches.observation: Inference clients use discovery bases unchanged; the documented per-family path segments are missing. Existing aliases may work, but current docs do not establish them.
mismatches.test: Assert exact URL per preset and protocol while retaining discovery /models bases.

mismatches.title: OpenCode gateway authentication mismatch
mismatches.observation: Messages rotates SDK api_key and native Gemini sends x-goog-api-key. The gateway's explicit requirement is Bearer; alternate header acceptance is undocumented.
mismatches.test: Capture exact headers at actual HTTP boundary for all gateway families and retained session metadata.

mismatches.title: Go native Gemini routing gap
mismatches.observation: Go lacks a Gemini family rule although the official current table lists a Google-native Gemini contributor route. Discovery-supplied protocol metadata can override this, so impact depends on metadata.
mismatches.test: Check sparse/manual model setup plus explicit provider protocol metadata without guessing upstream URLs.

mismatches.title: Responses native continuation lost
mismatches.observation: The adapter rebuilds text/functions and does not retain complete output items or a previous-response chain, losing opaque reasoning and provider fields.
mismatches.test: Round-trip completed reasoning+function items, preserve ordering/identities, and reject required missing metadata.

mismatches.title: Responses terminal failures normalized as length
mismatches.observation: response.failed and all incomplete reasons become length; explicit error events are ignored and EOF is accepted. Server failures are distinct from max_output_tokens.
mismatches.test: Fixture failed/server_error, incomplete/max_output_tokens, refusal/filter reason, explicit error, and missing terminal.

mismatches.title: Reasoning replay limited by model-name heuristic
mismatches.observation: Only DeepSeek/Kimi names with tools trigger scalar reasoning replay, and the original field key is lost. This misses documented preserved-thinking cases, including Kimi without tools and Together reasoning-key retention.
mismatches.test: Test native reasoning key and whole-message preservation across tool and ordinary assistant turns; retain strict provider/model identity checks.

mismatches.title: Mistral typed content unsupported
mismatches.observation: Current parsing assumes string delta content and passes nonstream lists through without separating thinking. Mistral documents ThinkChunk/TextChunk lists and mixed transition chunks.
mismatches.test: Feed text, thinking, mixed transition and tool parts through actual HTTP/SDK parsing and keep private reasoning out of visible narration.

mismatches.title: Cache accounting ignores Together flat field
mismatches.observation: Only nested cached_tokens is read; Together documents usage.cached_tokens on some models.
mismatches.test: Exercise nested and flat cache usage in streamed and complete responses without inventing missing usage.

mismatches.title: Streaming transport completion needs raw boundary proof
mismatches.observation: The SDK iterator's EOF currently counts as completion. Kimi requires [DONE]; OpenRouter's midstream error can be the only frame. SDK event handling may hide markers or raise errors, so prove this at HTTP/SSE level.
mismatches.test: Test stop-then-EOF without DONE, full DONE, final usage repetition, and error-only HTTP200.

mismatches.title: Retry-After and permanent 429 classification
mismatches.observation: Server Retry-After is capped by max_delay and retained only for 429. Current OpenAI docs require respecting it for 503 too; billing/spend 429 differs from temporary rate limits.
mismatches.test: Test long numeric/HTTP-date Retry-After without real sleeping, cancellation while waiting, 503 hints and nonrecoverable billing codes.

mismatches.title: Responses tool options need translation/preservation
mismatches.observation: Function conversion drops strict; kwargs passthrough does not translate nested Chat named tool_choice or response_format to Responses text.format. A deliberate strict:false can therefore change meaning.
mismatches.test: Fixture required/none/named choice, strict:false retention, and text.format translation. Gateway strict-default details remain undocumented.

Reliability guide says transient retry; error-code table says likely server bug. Bounded retry and clear failure retain both.
